title: United Arab Republic
capsule: The United Arab Republic was proclaimed on 1 February 1958 when Egypt and Syria merged under President Gamal Abdel Nasser, who had proposed the union in response to requests by Syrian officers and Ba'athists seeking protection against communism and conservative neighbors. Cairo served as capital, with Egypt as the "Southern Region" and Syria the "Northern Region," but the union rapidly became Egyptian-dominated: Syrian political parties were dissolved, Egyptian officers filled command posts, and agrarian reforms damaged Syrian commercial agriculture. Syrian army officers staged a coup on 28 September 1961 and declared independence; Nasser accepted the fait accompli rather than attempt reconquest. Egypt continued to use the name United Arab Republic until Anwar Sadat formally renamed the state the Arab Republic of Egypt on 2 September 1971.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory is precisely defined as Egypt plus Syria 1958–1961, and Egypt alone from 1961 to the formal name change in 1971; the dataset's to-year of 1973 may reflect continued use of the name in some diplomatic contexts.
